headline: High: ECC’s writable, networked workspace can conflict with ai-engineering-hub’s MCP/RAG-oriented outputs, creating default data-flow and action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is tagged for MCP/RAG and may emit content consumed by ECC, while ECC explicitly uses MCP, skills, and stdin/stdout plus writable config files. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if ECC treats imported content as trusted. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF ECC ingests ai-engineering-hub-generated text into skills, hooks, or MCP prompts without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are bridged by copy-paste or shared files, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic import of generated text into ECC skills/hooks.
Add a provenance label to any ai-engineering-hub output before reuse.
Review MCP inputs for instruction-like content before execution.
Use a separate staging file for copied content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or provenance enforcement in the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC reads and writes local files, session data, and MCP configs, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent repository with no filesystem surface shown. If both are run on the same machine or workspace, ECC can expose local artifacts that ai-engineering-hub content may reference or summarize. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or repository checkout, ECC can read files that ai-engineering-hub workflows may process.
IF ECC uploads file contents through allowlisted network APIs, local artifacts can leave the machine.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories.
Exclude secrets from any shared workspace.
Turn off file ingestion for nonessential runs.
Audit ECC uploads before enabling networked workflows.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and network egress; ai-engineering-hub is an agent repo that may be used as a source of prompts or code. If both operate on the same checkout, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite changes. Because ECC explicitly supports multiple instances and shared state warnings, the conflict is credible and defaults can be dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git checkout, commits or working-tree edits can race.
IF ECC runs multiple instances against the same root, session or config files can be overwritten.
mitigations: Use separate git clones per agent.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Set distinct roots for each instance.
Review git diffs before any commit.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s skills and MCP workflow can treat upstream content as operational input, while ai-engineering-hub is a repository of agent patterns and examples. If ECC consumes ai-engineering-hub outputs without verification, mistakes can cascade into generated skills, configs, or actions. The pairwise dependency is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ECC uses ai-engineering-hub output as authoritative input, errors can propagate into downstream actions.
IF generated instructions are converted into skills or hooks without review, bad advice becomes persistent.
mitigations: Require human review before promoting outputs to skills or hooks.
Compare outputs against source docs before execution.
Keep a rollback copy of prior configs.
Limit automation to read-only analysis runs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings. The only concrete compliance concern is that ECC stores operational metadata locally; without a second documented regime for ai-engineering-hub, the pairwise compliance gap is limited and uncertain. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair’s combined handling.
conditions: IF ECC is configured to retain sessions longer than the operator’s policy, retention mismatch arises.
IF ai-engineering-hub content includes regulated data and is copied into ECC, local handling obligations may apply.
mitigations: Shorten ECC retention settings.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts.
Document which data classes may enter ECC.
Review local logs for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both tools.
